Title: Account lockout never triggered — failed login counter reset on every attempt
StepsToReproduce:
1. POST /api/auth/login for employee7@example.com with a wrong password 5 times.
2. POST /api/auth/login with the correct password.
ExpectedResult: The account locks after 5 failures (423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED) and the correct password is refused while the lock is active.
ActualResult: Every attempt returned 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS and the correct password then returned 200 — brute-force protection was ineffective.
Evidence: test-evidence/logs/api.txt · tests/api/auth.spec.ts “five failed attempts lock the account”
RootCause: lib/authenticate.js treated a NULL locked_until as an expired lock window, so nextAttemptState() returned 0 on every attempt and failed_count never reached the 5-attempt threshold.
RetestResult: Pass — 5 failures return 423, the following correct password still returns 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED.
RegressionResult: Pass — the whole auth.spec.ts file and the UI lockout test (HR-TC-010) pass after the fix.
Rationale: Security-relevant defect: without a working lockout an attacker can brute-force the seeded demo accounts indefinitely.

Title: Attendance with status ABSENT accepted check-in/check-out times
ExpectedResult: 422 INVALID_ATTENDANCE_PAYLOAD — an absent employee has no working hours (only PRESENT/REMOTE rows carry times).
ActualResult: 201 Created — an ABSENT row was stored with working hours, contradicting the documented rule.
RootCause: validation.js assertAttendanceRules only rejected times for LEAVE and only required them for PRESENT/REMOTE, leaving ABSENT unconstrained.
RetestResult: Pass — ABSENT with times returns 422 INVALID_ATTENDANCE_PAYLOAD.
RegressionResult: Pass — attendance create/update suites and the seeded-data SQL checks still pass (no seeded ABSENT row carries times).
Rationale: Data quality: inconsistent attendance rows would corrupt the attendance-rate report.

Title: Malformed email on /api/auth/login answered 401 instead of 400
ExpectedResult: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with a field-level detail for email.
ActualResult: 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS — client-side input errors were reported as authentication failures, which also hides genuine typos from the user.
RootCause: loginSchema accepted any string as email; the format check happened nowhere.
RetestResult: Pass — malformed email returns 400 with details[].path = "email".
RegressionResult: Pass — the whole auth suite (API + UI) still passes.
Rationale: Correct status codes keep the contract testable and make client-side errors distinguishable from credential errors.

Title: POST /api/attendance had no authorization check — any role could write attendance for anybody
StepsToReproduce:
1. Sign in as employee1@example.com.
2. POST /api/attendance with { "employeeId": 4, "workDate": "2026-01-05", "status": "PRESENT", "checkIn": "09:00", "checkOut": "17:00" }.
3. Repeat as manager@example.com with employeeId 1.
ExpectedResult: 403 FORBIDDEN in both cases — an EMPLOYEE cannot write attendance at all and a MANAGER only for self + direct reports.
ActualResult: 201 Created in both cases — a vertical and horizontal privilege escalation: salary-relevant attendance data could be forged by any authenticated user.
Evidence: test-evidence/logs/api.txt · assertions “attendanceWrite.status() to be 403” and “outOfScope.status() to be 403”
RootCause: services.createAttendance() never called canWriteAttendance(); only the PATCH route checked permissions.
RetestResult: Pass — EMPLOYEE 403, MANAGER 403 outside the team, 201 inside the team, terminated employee 422.
RegressionResult: Pass — the full RBAC matrix (7 tests) and the attendance suite pass after the fix.
Rationale: Broken object/function-level authorization is the highest-impact class of defect in an HR system; it also proved the value of testing every role against every endpoint.

Title: Signing in after a redirect never returned to the requested page
StepsToReproduce:
1. Open /employees while signed out (the app redirects to /login?next=%2Femployees).
2. Submit valid HR credentials.
ActualResult: The login page was re-rendered with “Enter a valid email address and password.” — the hidden `next` field was rejected by the strict credential schema (400) and the deep link never worked.
RootCause: pages.js POST /login passed the whole form body (including next) to a .strict() schema.
RetestResult: Pass — after signing in the browser lands on the requested page.
RegressionResult: Pass — all five login UI tests pass.
Rationale: The redirect-after-login path is a common entry point (shared bookmarks, expired sessions) and silently failing it looks like broken credentials.

Title: Employee list page returned 400 when a filter was left empty
StepsToReproduce:
1. Open /employees.
2. Type a name into the search box and press Apply (or submit with “All departments” selected).
ActualResult: A validation error page: departmentId= (empty string) was coerced to 0 and rejected by the positive-integer rule, so the most common user action on the page failed.
Evidence: test-evidence/logs/ui.txt · page snapshot showing VALIDATION_ERROR “departmentId: Number must be greater than 0”
RootCause: req.query was validated as-is; HTML forms always submit every control, including empty selects.
RetestResult: Pass — empty filters are treated as “no filter” and the list renders.
RegressionResult: Pass — employees UI suite (7 tests) and the API filter matrix still pass; API validation stays strict for real values.
Rationale: Highest user-visible impact of the run: search/filter/pagination — the core list workflow — was unusable.

Title: Signed-in user name rendered as “undefined undefined” in the header
StepsToReproduce: 1. Sign in as any role and read the header next to the role badge.
ExpectedResult: The full name of the signed-in employee, e.g. “Amara Okafor”.
RootCause: toPublicActor() formatted first_name/last_name while the session middleware passes camelCase fields.
RetestResult: Pass — the header shows the real full name for every role.
RegressionResult: Pass — the login UI suite passes; screenshots show real names.
Rationale: Cosmetic but immediately visible; it also proved the API shape and the session shape had drifted apart.

Title: Deleting an employee with audit history failed with HTTP 500
StepsToReproduce:
1. Create an employee, sign in as them and submit a leave request (so they are the actor of an audit row).
2. As ADMIN: DELETE /api/employees/:id.
ExpectedResult: 204 No Content — child rows cascade and the audit trail survives.
ActualResult: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR — FOREIGN KEY constraint failed on audit_logs.actor_id (no ON DELETE action), so employees who had ever acted in the system could never be deleted.
DetectedBy: Postman collection (09 · Cleanup) — confirmed with a dedicated API test
Evidence: test-evidence/logs/postman.txt · assertion “ADMIN deletes the fixture employee - expected 204 but got 500”
RootCause: audit_logs.actor_id and leave_requests.reviewed_by referenced employees(id) without an ON DELETE action.
RetestResult: Pass — 204, attendance/leave rows cascade, LEAVE_CREATE audit row survives with actorId null.
RegressionResult: Pass — employees suite including the new regression test (HR-TC-022) plus the SQL orphan checks (DB-10).
Rationale: Unhandled 500s on a core admin action, and a nice example of one suite (Postman) catching what unit-level API tests missed.

Title: Automation: employee fixtures collided because each Playwright worker restarted the counter
StepsToReproduce: 1. Run the API suite: several spec files generate employee codes from a module-level counter starting at 1.
ExpectedResult: Every generated EMP code is unique across the whole run.
ActualResult: Codes repeated (EMP-801 in several files) and the create calls returned 409 DUPLICATE_EMPLOYEE_CODE, producing false failures.
DetectedBy: Playwright API suite (11 red tests in the first full run)
RootCause: Playwright isolates each test file in its own worker process, so module state is not shared.
RetestResult: Pass — 57/57 API tests green after seeding the counter from the process start time.
RegressionResult: Pass — repeated full runs are stable.
Rationale: Recorded because test-code defects produce the same false signals as product defects; keeping them in the log shows the difference.

Title: Automation: SQL check computed “tomorrow” in UTC and accepted today’s date
StepsToReproduce: 1. Run tests/db/06-seed-and-api-integration.mjs in a timezone ahead of UTC.
ExpectedResult: The future-hire negative probe is rejected with 422.
ActualResult: 201 Created — new Date(Date.now()+86400000).toISOString() was still “today” locally, so the probe was not in the future and the check failed for the wrong reason.
Evidence: test-evidence/logs/db.txt · “Expected values to be strictly equal: 201 !== 422”
RootCause: Mixing UTC (toISOString) with the application’s local-calendar date rules.
RetestResult: Pass — the check uses the application’s own addDays(todayIso(), 1) helper.
Rationale: A timezone bug in the test could easily have been reported as an application bug; the defect log documents the triage.

Title: Automation: UNIQUE index probe searched sqlite_master.sql and found nothing
StepsToReproduce: 1. Run the SQL validation suite (check DB-01).
ExpectedResult: The attendance UNIQUE(employee_id, work_date) index is detected.
ActualResult: Check failed: table-level UNIQUE constraints create auto-indexes whose sqlite_master.sql column is NULL, so the LIKE-based probe could not see them.
Evidence: test-evidence/logs/db.txt · “attendance must carry a UNIQUE index on (employee_id, work_date)”
RootCause: Wrong introspection method for implicit indexes.
RetestResult: Pass — PRAGMA index_list + PRAGMA index_info confirm the unique pair.
Rationale: Shows the value of validating the validator before trusting a red result.

Title: Session of a terminated employee stayed valid until expiry
StepsToReproduce:
1. Sign in as an employee and keep the cookie/token.
2. As ADMIN set that employee status = TERMINATED.
3. Call any endpoint with the old session.
ExpectedResult: The session is revoked (401) because the account no longer exists in an active state.
ActualResult: The old session kept working for read endpoints (and would have kept working for the rest of the 8 hour lifetime of the token) — the middleware only checked the expiry, never the account status.
DetectedBy: Exploratory charter HR-EX-05 (session and cookie abuse)
RootCause: middleware/auth.js loaded the session join without inspecting employees.status.
RetestResult: Pass — the stale token returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and the sessions row is deleted on the first request.
RegressionResult: Pass — HR-TC-050 and the whole authentication suite pass; the “leave of a terminated employee cannot be reviewed” rule still returns 422 for the manager.
Rationale: Account termination is an offboarding control; leaving the session alive undermines it (the classic “terminated but still logged in” finding from HR self-service systems).

Title: SEEDED — MANAGER employee list is not scoped (broken object level authorization)
StepsToReproduce:
1. Start the app with SEED_DEFECTS=1.
2. Sign in as manager@example.com.
3. GET /api/employees?limit=100.
ExpectedResult: Only the manager and their seven direct reports are returned.
ActualResult: All ten employees of the company are returned, including ADMIN and HR — while the detail endpoint still answers 403, which makes the leak easy to miss manually.
RootCause: Injected: lib/queries.js bypasses the scope helper when the flag is on (documented in lib/seed-defects.js).
RetestResult: n/a — injected defect, must fail with SEED_DEFECTS=1 and pass with 0.
RegressionResult: Clean runs (SEED_DEFECTS=0) prove the guard is in place; the detection script fails as expected when enabled.
Rationale: Demonstrates that a green detail endpoint does not prove the list endpoint is scoped.

Title: SEEDED — leave overlap guard skips requests that start on the same day
StepsToReproduce:
1. Start the app with SEED_DEFECTS=1.
2. Sign in as employee6@example.com (EMP-009 owns the seeded PENDING request today+10 → today+12).
3. POST /api/leave-requests with exactly those dates.
ActualResult: 201 Created — an off-by-one in the overlap guard lets an employee double-book the same window when the start date matches.
RootCause: Injected: services.js skips the overlap result when start_date matches exactly (documented in lib/seed-defects.js).
RetestResult: n/a — injected defect, must fail with SEED_DEFECTS=1 and pass with 0.
RegressionResult: The overlap boundary cases (HR-TC-045/046) pass on clean runs.
Rationale: Boundary-style off-by-one bugs are the classic case for date-range test design.
